title: Compound Angle Identities & Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions (AA HL)

questions.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\tan x}$.
questions.answer: $\sec x - \cos x = \frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}$. Dividing by $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ gives $\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \sin x$.

questions.q: Which identity relates $\cot\theta$ and $\csc\theta$ for all defined angles?
questions.answer: Dividing $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ by $\sin^2\theta$ yields the fundamental Pythagorean identity $1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta$.

questions.q: Use compound angle identities to find the exact value of $\cos(75^{\circ}) = \cos(45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ})$.

questions.answer: Using the subtraction formula $\sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B$ with $A = x + y$ and $B = y$, this simplifies to $\sin((x + y) - y) = \sin x$.

questions.q: If $\tan A = 2$ and $\tan B = 3$, what is $\tan(A + B)$?
If $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is acute, what is $\cos(2\theta)$?
Under the same conditions ($\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ acute), what is $\sin(2\theta)$?
Express $\cos^2 x$ in terms of a first-power cosine function.
Express $3\sin x + 4\cos x$ in the form $R\sin(x + \alpha)$ with $R > 0$ and $0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}$.
questions.answer: $R = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$. Expand $R\sin(x + \alpha) = R\cos\alpha \sin x + R\sin\alpha \cos x$. Thus $R\cos\alpha = 3$ and $R\sin\alpha = 4 \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = 4/3 \Rightarrow \alpha = \arctan(4/3) \approx 0.927\text{ rad}$.

questions.q: What is the maximum value of the function $f(x) = 5\cos x - 12\sin x + 3$?
questions.answer: The combination $5\cos x - 12\sin x$ has amplitude $R = \sqrt{5^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$. The maximum value is $13 + 3 = 16$.
